summary: A companion app can become an expensive, persuasive cache of outdated interpretations. Its broad integrations also create a concentrated security boundary and can overwhelm rather than orient newcomers.

points.text: Generated summaries may lag code, deployments, or decisions and still look authoritative. A stale companion can be more dangerous than missing documentation because users stop checking the source.

To connect code, tickets, traces, incidents, and decisions, the app often receives wider read access than any normal developer tool; indexing and search can unintentionally expose secrets or restricted operational data.
Large dependency maps and undifferentiated timelines increase cognitive load. Controlled evidence suggests that representation benefits are task-specific rather than universal.
Generation, indexing, identity integration, link repair, and schema evolution create a standing platform cost that may exceed the value for small or rapidly changing systems.
